key_insight: An ion-pumped SrFeO3-δ thin film can reversibly switch between brownmillerite and perovskite phases, enabling continuous analog control of optical transmittance and color.
engineering_relevance: This suggests oxygen-based mixed ionic-electronic conductors could serve as low-power, nonvolatile optical modulators compatible with oxide electronics and silicon photonics.
method: Reversible oxygen-driven phase transitions in SrFeO3-δ thin films
Integration of an optically passive Al2O3 interference layer
Optical modulation via ion-induced structural and electronic changes
evidence_signal: The abstract reports pronounced changes in electronic structure and optical constants, with continuous and reversible transmittance and color modulation after phase switching.
watch_item: Practical deployment may still face challenges in switching speed, voltage, and long-term cycling stability despite the improved materials platform.
paper_title: Structure-driven analog optical control in ion-pumped SrFeO$_{3-δ}$ thin-film devices
